hypothesis: Without retuning, AuroraPIC using the previously locked Maiorov 2024 analytic argon cross-section package predicts drift velocities derived from independent Dutton high-field mobility measurements within 20% plus two simulation standard errors at every exactly matched measured field.

selection_contract.rule: For each source and target, select its single nearest positive-field observation only if abs(measured-target)/target <= 0.10; ties select the lower field.

aligned: argon electron mobility/drift under a uniform reduced electric field
exact measured reduced fields without interpolation
cross sections and numerical settings fixed before observing the comparison
known_ambiguities: Dutton describes these source groups as ambient temperature unless otherwise stated; the three selected source blocks do not state an exact gas temperature
the historical mobility records do not identify the modern flux-versus-bulk transport convention
the LXCat transcription does not provide pointwise experimental uncertainties

data_governance: The LXCat export and locally derived point table remain under tmp/ and are not redistributed. The committed preparer, cryptographic hashes, selection contract, and aggregate result permit auditing without republishing contributor data.
classification: Passing is evidence that this untuned argon collision package is consistent with three historical experimental sources at the declared engineering tolerance. Failure identifies a physical-model discrepancy, not by itself a PIC-kernel defect, because the published-fit collision package and historical coefficient conventions are separate uncertainty sources.
claim_boundary: This comparison validates only homogeneous argon electron transport. It does not validate ion transport, self-consistent fields, boundaries, geometry, plasma chemistry, or a complete device calculation. Exact temperature and bulk/flux ambiguity prevent a metrology-grade validation claim.
